body:
These attacks can target web applications and their underlying infrastructure, leading to the unintended leakage of sensitive information. Considering the potential security risks that side-channel attacks pose, I propose that ASVS should include an item to address that.

**Example:**

An online messaging web application uses a JavaScript cryptographic library to perform RSA encryption and decryption. The library's implementation of modular exponentiation contains timing leaks due to secret-dependent branches and loop iterations. An attacker with access to another browser window or service worker running malicious code could perform a cache-timing attack to exploit these leaks.

By analyzing the differences in execution time for various operations, the attacker may be able to reveal the encrypted messages or even private keys. This would compromise the confidentiality and integrity of the messages exchanged between users on the platform. (inspired by a [real world scenario](https://github.com/andyperlitch/jsbn/issues/43))

Proposed ASVS check:

_Verify that the application has implemented appropriate countermeasures to protect against side-channel attacks._

**Mitigation:**
- Implement constant-time algorithms for sensitive operations.
- Add random delays to the application's responses or processing times to make it more difficult for attackers to measure timing differences accurately.
